clue.text: Reach the others and stop

parts.note: to reach a place is to come to it
the rest means the others, those remaining

explanation.surface: Someone catches up with the rest of the group and halts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes to rest has halted, so the phrase is a synonym for stopping.

clue.text: Forget to order vermouth

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A barman fails to put in an order for vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command to buy, but it is the Order of Merit (OM), a British honour; 'It' is the old bar name for Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, as one does on forgetting it.

clue.text: No more wine — that's the limit

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer so
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone told the wine has run out declares that the last straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's the limit' sounds like exasperation; 'limit' alone is the definition. TENT is a dark red wine from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The extent of something is how far it reaches, its bounds or scope.

clue.text: Not doing well, removed from the class

parts.note: something taken off has been removed
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A pupil struggling at lessons is taken out of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a class or year group in a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: A player or performer off form is below their usual standard, performing poorly.

clue.text: Take a meal up for girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to dine is to take a meal

explanation.surface: An invitation to bring dinner upstairs for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' in a down clue reverses DINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a girl's name, so a girl can stand for it in crosswords.

clue.text: Traitor's initial justification for his crime

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, here taken from traitor's

parts.note: a reason is a justification for an action

explanation.surface: A traitor's first excuse for what he did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial justification' tempts as a phrase, but 'initial' belongs to 'Traitor's' and gives its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is the offence a traitor commits, so his crime is this.

clue.text: Indulgent client settles debts

indicators.note: settles suggests the letters of client being rearranged into a new order

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A customer pays off what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles' looks like paying, but it rearranges CLIENT into LICENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Licentious means unrestrained in pleasures, giving way to every desire, which is self-indulgent.

clue.text: Clashing of gears gives offensive result

indicators.note: clashing suggests the letters of gears and gives grinding into a new order

explanation.surface: Grinding gears makes a horrible noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' reads as unpleasant, but it is the definition in its sense of attacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive and offensive both describe being on the attack, ready to strike first.

clue.text: Part of a building-birds may be on it

explanation.surface: An extension where birds might perch.
explanation.definitionFit: A side section of a large building is one sense; birds flying are said to be on it, airborne.

clue.text: The living present?

parts.note: read not as the here and now but as a gift that is life itself, the present of being alive

explanation.definitionFit: Life given, through birth or a donated organ, is a present of being alive.

clue.text: A new paper to be published

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of paper are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh newspaper is about to go to press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new paper' reads as a fresh newspaper, but 'new' is the anagram signal working on 'paper'; 'to' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A book is said to come out or be issued when published, and these all mean the same.

clue.text: Acts for different agents

indicators.note: different suggests the letters of acts for take another order

explanation.surface: Someone stands in on behalf of various representatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a commercial agent who buys and sells for others.

clue.text: Where one may find a small jumper with a big top?

definitions.text: Where one may find a small jumper with a big top?

parts.words: Where one may find a small jumper with a big top?
parts.note: the jumper is not a sweater but a tiny leaping insect, and the big top is a circus tent, not clothing

explanation.definitionFit: A show of trained tiny insects performing tricks under a miniature tent.

clue.text: Frank gains the new seat-these wanted it too!

parts.note: frank and candid both mean open and honest

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of seat are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An honest politician wins the new constituency, though others coveted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' is both the anagram fodder and, in the surface, the parliamentary seat the rivals wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: People standing for election all hope to win the contested place.

clue.text: It's an odd sort of stuff

indicators.note: an odd sort of suggests the letters of it's an are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: A remark that something is a strange kind of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is the old word for woven cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for fabric, and this is a smooth glossy fabric.

clue.text: Places drawn roughly to scale

indicators.note: drawn roughly suggests the letters of to scale are sketched out in a loose new order

explanation.surface: Locations on a map sketched only approximately to scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn roughly' sounds like map-making but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to find where it is, a verb sense shared here.

clue.text: He won't win new roles

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of roles appear in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An actor given different parts is not going to win an award.
explanation.definitionFit: One who comes off worst in a contest is beaten, never the victor.

clue.text: Builder of a lodge

parts.note: both a worker in stone who might build a lodge and a member of a ... lodge

explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker builds walls, and a Freemason belongs to a lodge.

clue.text: Bird from another nest

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run another nest

explanation.surface: A bird that came from a different nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea eagle, a large bird of prey much used in crosswords.

clue.text: Withdrawal of 101 meeting points

indicators.note: withdrawal means drawing back, so the word of is turned round

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Pulling out of course 101 at the gathering places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawal' reverses OF to FO; 101 is CI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is a point where lines or rays converge, so the plural is points of meeting.

clue.text: One having two members in support

definitions.text: One having two members in support

parts.words: One having two members in support
parts.note: the members are not of a club but limbs, a pair of legs holding the body up

explanation.definitionFit: Humans and birds walk on two legs, which support them.

clue.text: Attitude taken by a navigator

explanation.surface: A posture adopted by a ship's navigator.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing means posture or manner; a navigator also takes a compass direction of this name.

clue.text: Abandons lands in the sea

explanation.surface: A pilot gives up and brings the aircraft down on water.
explanation.definitionFit: To get rid of something is one sense; a pilot also does this when forced down onto water.

clue.text: Yellow bird

explanation.surface: A canary-coloured bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow means cowardly, as does this word; it is also a domestic fowl.

clue.text: A quick reply showing wit or spite perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of or spite may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A sharp retort can be clever or malicious.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp clever retort, originally a fencer's counter-thrust.

clue.text: City's side at sea in scoreless draw

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a nil-nil draw is written 0-0, read as two Os
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A town's team plays out a goalless draw by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A scoreless draw, 0-0, gives two Os with PORT inside. Oporto is the English name for Porto in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese city of Porto, also called Oporto, is a port-wine centre.

clue.text: Standard text-book for a senior lecturer

explanation.surface: The set book written by a senior academic.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a READER is a senior lecturer, one rank below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory school anthology is one sense; a senior academic grade in Britain is the other.

clue.text: Final passage of hoax article

parts.note: cod means a hoax or sham, as in cod Latin
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The last part of a fake piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: COD is British slang for fake or a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a coda is the closing section that rounds off a piece.

clue.text: Strikers attempt to get a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word stab is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a stab is an attempt

explanation.surface: Workers on strike try to win a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' and 'rise' suggest industrial action, but strikers are cricket or baseball bats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats are what hit the ball in cricket or baseball, so they strike.

clue.text: Hailstorm breaks out around the East-it's to do with temperature

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
breaks out suggests the hailstorm's letters bursting into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A hailstorm erupts in the east, a matter of weather and temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks out' rearranges HAILSTORM, and 'around' puts that round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Isothermal means at constant heat or relating to equal heat levels.

clue.text: Employer provides a course in the City

annotationWithheld.why: Employer provides a course in the City (4), answer USER: 'Employer' defines it, but no reading of 'provides a course in the City' builds USER and no search found the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Employer provides a course in the City

clue.text: Where they try to force soldiers to be good?

definitions.text: Where they try to force soldiers to be good?

parts.words: Where they try to force soldiers to be good?
parts.note: forcing is what gardeners do to plants under glass, and also the army jail where soldiers are disciplined

explanation.definitionFit: A greenhouse forces plants, and in British army slang it is a military prison.
